title: Customer Network Safety KPIs and Compact Audit Hypotheses
body:
TL;DR: Draft a compact, operationally-actionable set of safety KPIs and audit hypotheses for customer-managed networking (VPC / on-prem) that balances forensic fidelity with storage/query cost. Propose a lightweight audit envelope ("evidence capsule") format, sampling rules for change events, operator UX hooks for rapid rollback, and measurable SLAs for approval gates. Prioritize: (1) forensic triage speed, (2) probability of having sufficient evidence for rollbacks/PD, (3) customer privacy and minimal egress, (4) bounded storage cost per customer.

Context / problem statement:
- Private deployments mean many networking changes occur outside Redwood's infra (customer-controlled firewalls, peering, NAT changes, operator scripts). When incidents happen we have limited visibility and must rely on compact telemetry and customer-provided artifacts.
- Existing PRD drafts focus on exhaustive attestation ledgers and long retention; customers push back on data egress, retention, and legal complexity. We need a middle path: deterministic, small audit payloads that enable triage and automated rollback without full packet-level telemetry.

Goals (what success looks like):
- KPI-1: Mean time to triage (MTT) for network-change incidents <= 25 minutes for incidents where evidence capsule exists.
- KPI-2: Probability that a random critical change (as defined by our risk model) has a usable evidence capsule >= 85% at GA.
- KPI-3: Average storage per tenant for audit envelope <= 5 MB/day (configurable by tier).
- KPI-4: Approval gate latency 95th percentile <= 300ms for automated pre-checks; human approval median <= 4 minutes when reviewers alerted.
- KPI-5: Rollback fidelity (ability to restore a previous known-good config without customer intervention) >= 70% for operator-initiated rollbacks where capsule exists.

Key concepts and proposed artifacts:
1) Evidence capsule (compact audit envelope):
   - Purpose: single-file, cryptographically-signed bundle capturing minimal data needed to reason about a change and perform a rollback or reconstruct intent.
   - Suggested fields (compact): version, change_id, actor_id (pseudonymized/hashed if required), timestamp, change_type (route/table/peering/firewall/nat), delta (compact diff), pre_state_digest (hash of prior config), optional snapshot pointer (if customer allows full snapshot), operator-comment (free text), approval_proof (signed approval token), sampling_flag, schema_version.
   - Size budget: aim for < 50KB per typical change when snapshot omitted.
   - Storage/retention: default 90 days for evidence capsule metadata + 7 days for attached snapshots (tiered).

2) Sampling and heuristics:
   - Always-capture events: creation/destruction of peering, route table replacements, public egress rule openings, operator-initiated mass changes (> N rules), and any change that matches risk rules.
   - Probabilistic sampling: small config tweaks (single rule edits) sampled at 10% by default. Sample rate configurable by customer or by Redwood policy.
   - Adaptive sampling: ramp up sampling (to 100%) if system detects repeated failures from same actor or an increase in error surface.
   - Rationale: reduces storage; keeps high signal for high-risk changes.

3) Approval gates and pre-checks:
   - Preflight static checks run in Redwood control-plane (local simulation against recent capsule digest): conflict detection, route blackhole detection, egress leak heuristics, overlapping CIDR warnings, permit/deny precedence anomalies. Preflight should fail-fast and return clear human-friendly hints.
   - Automated approvals allowed for low-risk changes with past successful rollout history; otherwise require 1 human approver. Use canary windows and auto-revert triggers.
   - Approval SLAs and alerting: allow teams to set their own approval windows and escalation paths; Redwood sends structured evidence capsule with notification to approvers (Slack/email webhook).

4) Operator UX for incident response:
   - Search-first UI: query by change_id, actor_id, time window, CIDR, or impacted subnet. Capsules indexed by digest and tags.
   - One-click rollback: reconstruct delta from capsule and offer a "revert candidate" that can be applied with optional dry-run. Show expected impact and confidence score.
   - Forensic timeline: visualize sequence of capsules and system metrics around the change (CPU, connection drops, application error spikes if telemetry provided).

5) Privacy and minimal egress model:
   - Capsule fields default to pseudonymized actor_id; full identity resolved only with customer opt-in or during joint incident review.
   - Snapshots and richer telemetry require explicit customer consent and per-capsule authorization.

6) Compact data model and query patterns:
   - Use columnar store for capsule metadata and object store for capsule payloads. Keep payloads compressed (brotli) and index top-level fields for fast retrieval.
   - Query patterns to optimize: change_id lookup, actor/time range, impacted-subnet search (precompute inverted index), risk-score filtering.

Rollout proposal (phased):
- Phase 0 (experiment): implement capsule v0 collector + local dry-run preflight. Test with 3 pilot customers (SaaS, fintech, health) focusing on capture and rollback UX.
- Phase 1 (beta): sampling controls + adaptive sampling + basic UI for search/rollback. Retention: 30-day metadata.
- Phase 2 (GA): full approval integration, configurable retention tiers, SLA-backed approval latency, integration with KMS for capsule signing.

Operational and cost considerations:
- Storage budget caps per tenant with tiered pricing; alert when approaching cap and provide auto-archive option.
- For high-volume tenants, prefer sampling + on-demand full-snapshot request.
- Encryption and signing: use customer-managed KMS when available; otherwise Redwood-managed keys with strict access controls and audit logging.

Open questions / tradeoffs (needs decisions quickly):
- Q1: Default sampling rates by change_type (we propose 100% for peering/egress open, 10% for single-rule edits). Product decision needed.
- Q2: Legal/retention constraints for regulated verticals — default 90 days may be insufficient (health/finance); should we offer longer as part of enterprise package?
- Q3: Should actor_id hashing be reversible by Redwood for root-cause analysis, or require customer-provided resolution keys?
- Q4: Snapshot pull vs push model: who initiates when a deeper snapshot is needed during triage? Push increases egress risk.

Monitoring & success measurement (launch metrics):
- Adoption: % of pilot tenants enabling capsules within first 60 days. Target >= 60% for pilots.
- Effectiveness: fraction of incidents where capsule enabled automated or semi-automated rollback. Target >= 50% in pilot.
- Cost: average daily storage per tenant and query latency P95 for lookup by change_id (target < 200ms).

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- [Product] Lock sampling defaults and retention tiers (decision by 2025-02-10).
- [Eng] Prototype capsule schema and brotli compression pipeline; expose sample API for partners (pr: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/47).
- [SE] Recruit 3 pilot customers and draft pilot runbook (owners: Diego Morales, Maya Singh).
- [Legal] Quick review of retention/transfer requirements for US/EU healthcare customers.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact — the goal is operational parity (fast triage + rollback) without exhaustive data exfiltration. Looking for feedback on sampling defaults, retention policy, and whether the capsule model meets typical SRE workflows.

- [ ] Document legal opt-in language for snapshot collection and retention exceptions.

End of doc.
